instructions:
Write a regex named `identifier` that matches a whole identifier: it **starts with a letter**, followed by **zero or more letters or digits**.

Use the character classes `[a-zA-Z]` and `[a-zA-Z0-9]`, anchor both ends, then log a few `.test()` results to check it. `count1` should match; `1count` and `my-var` should not.
hints: `^` anchors the start of the string and `$` anchors the end. Without them, `my-var` would match because it contains `my`.
The first character is exactly one letter: `^[a-zA-Z]`. Everything after it is `[a-zA-Z0-9]` repeated zero or more times — that's what `*` means.

tests.description: Anchors the start and requires a letter first
Allows zero or more letters or digits, anchored to the end
